briefing.opening: Hello. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 21, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and the Fury of El Niño
sections.content: As the global climate crisis deepens, the El Niño phenomenon is raging, causing widespread impacts [9, 29, 48]. Central and South America are experiencing severe water shortages due to El Niño-induced droughts, with the Panama Canal even drying up [9]. In Europe, heatwaves are rampant to the extent that Sicilian traditions are fading, and record early champagne harvests are occurring in French vineyards, demonstrating climate change's direct impact on agriculture and culture [43, 45, 47, 51, 52, 53, 55, 57]. Furthermore, the UK is preparing for extreme weather, with more autumn rain and storms forecast due to what is described as the 'biggest El Niño in a century,' having already experienced disruptions to railway services this summer due to heatwaves [60, 62]. This series of phenomena delivers a strong warning that the climate change we are currently experiencing is not a new normal, but merely the beginning [46].

sections.title: 🌱 Republic of Korea: Climate Change Response Efforts and Policy Shifts
sections.content: The Republic of Korea is strengthening its policy and practical efforts to address climate change. In the National Assembly, seven climate, energy, and environment bills have passed, accelerating the major transition to renewable energy [17]. Extensive reforms to related systems are being pursued, including the abolition of the Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) and priority grid connection for public-interest renewable energy [18, 19, 20]. Local governments are also actively responding to climate change. Gyeonggi Province is implementing 'climate-smart agriculture' to combat heatwaves, droughts, and pests [7]. Gokseong County is focusing on cultivating 'mandamgyu' (late-harvest citrus fruits), a promising crop for climate change adaptation, to explore new agricultural strategies [5]. Furthermore, there is growing interest in the impact of 'nature-based solutions,' which are spreading in overseas cities and regions, on domestic industries and policies [3]. A methodology for demonstrating climate resilience through sustainability disclosure scenario analysis has also been presented [6].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges of Energy Transition and Raising Social Awareness
sections.content: Challenges that need to be addressed in the transition to renewable energy are also clearly emerging. Korea faces a triple burden of limited land, constrained power grids, and public acceptance [22]. Bottlenecks in transmission networks and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are hindering the expansion of renewable energy [24]. Some argue that the limitations of renewable energy are evident, with 19 nuclear power plants included in mega-projects [25]. Meanwhile, a 'paradox of climate change' is observed, where new economic opportunities are created, such as the opening of the Arctic route, shortening the Busan-Europe sea route by 35% due to climate change [1, 2]. Amidst these complex circumstances, various efforts are being made to raise public awareness of climate change and encourage action. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism is operating a carbon-neutral pop-up experience center in conjunction with the popular webtoon 'Yumi's Cells' [10, 13, 14], and the Gyeongsan Carbon Neutrality Support Center is holding a seminar to present environmental education drafts [12, 15, 16].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Vulnerabilities and Warnings for the Future
sections.content: Globally, climate change is exposing various societal vulnerabilities. In several African countries, climate change is predicted to alter diarrhea prevalence, increasing the risk of diarrhea in children [33, 44]. Ecological threats are also intensifying, with a record 33 million tons of toxic seaweed covering Caribbean beaches [59]. In some regions, a regression in climate change awareness is observed. Concerns have been raised in Florida that climate change-related content was quietly removed from textbooks [39], and UK Labour MPs criticized the party for becoming complacent about the climate crisis, pointing to a lack of preparedness [30]. Furthermore, climate change acts as a factor exacerbating inflation, with predictions that it could triple wheat prices [34, 50]. Even new plans to address the water shortage crisis in the Colorado River in the US are deemed insufficient by experts [64]. Thus, climate change is not merely an environmental issue but poses unprecedented threats across all domains, including society, economy, and health, demanding our immediate and robust response.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, along with various domestic and international efforts and challenges to overcome it. This is a critical time when everyone's attention and action are urgently needed for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: The US Bureau of Reclamation released its proposal for a new 10-year plan on Friday to manage the future of the Colorado River, as the previous framework was set to expire in October.
summary.outlook: This plan mandates water cuts of up to 40% for California, Arizona, and Nevada. However, experts state that this plan alone may not be sufficient to avert the crisis.
